name: zlib-bitexact-rs (patched for level 4-9, memLevel 1-9) as the pure-Rust encoder-replay oracle
purpose: Bit-exact pure-Rust port of stock zlib 1.3.1 deflate_slow. With level and memLevel exposed (experiments/zbx_replay/patch_zbx.py) it is a drop-in replay oracle with stock zlib's exact behaviour, a challenger to preflate-rs's token predictor (TOOL-476/366) in WP-3.3 and WP-3.14.
verification_evidence: 2026-10-05: 400/400 Save As streams byte-exact (the OBS-0908 sample, including preflate-rs's 5 misses), memLevel sets equal stock zlib's on 800/800, 0/400 Print, no panics, 1.26-1.30x stock C zlib time (OBS-1100). The crate's own tests pass after the patch. Version, date, licence from crates.io (SRCH-1108); code read at commit ee337f437fe1 (SRC-1104, CLM-1105).
rationale: Upset of TOOL-476 for WP-3.3's product replay oracle: it matches stock zlib exactly (400/400 vs preflate-rs 395/400, OBS-1100 vs OBS-0908), needs no private-struct mirror, and with per-file self-calibration (OBS-1101) needs no producer profile. Not Adopt: the published API is fixed at level 9 / memLevel 8 (CLM-1105), so the product needs a fork or an upstream PR; only deflate_slow (levels 4-9, default strategy) is ported; the crate is 3 months old with one maintainer and 227 recent downloads. It is no help for Print to PDF (0/400), where preflate-rs's correction stream remains the only damage signal (OBS-0703).

name: Tesseract with per-script tessdata_best models (chi_sim, ara, hin, eng+fra+spa) as the OCR reference
purpose: Configuration of TOOL-382 for WP-3.2's OCR-of-render reference and WP-3.5's Document AI substitute: pick the traineddata by the page's script instead of -l eng.
version: tessdata_best main (sha256 per model in experiments/results/ocr_script_recall.tessdata.sha256); libtesseract 5.5.1 via tesserocr 2.11.0
license: Apache-2.0 (Tesseract and tessdata_best; from memory, not re-checked)
verification_evidence: 2026-10-05: on 24 REPDF Save As pages, per-script recall 0.938 Arabic, 0.889 Devanagari, 0.961 Han, 0.992 Latin vs -l eng 0.025, 0.035, 0.092, 0.982 (OBS-1102). Installed with pip into a scratch venv (tesserocr 2.11.0 wheel bundles libtesseract 5.5.1; PyPI metadata SRCH-1109).
rationale: Upset of the TOOL-382 configuration pinned in WP-3.2 (-l eng --psm 3): three of REPDF's six pages per document are non-Latin and -l eng recovers 2.5-9.2% of their characters (OBS-1102), so an -l eng reference makes REPDF-comparable recall on those pages meaningless. The language must come from the page's script; in REPDF the original's text layer gives the script, otherwise an unhinted multi-language run (0.81-0.91) or a script detector is needed. Trial, not Adopt: 24 pages, 4 documents, 200 dpi only; the 5.5.3 CLI of TOOL-382 was not re-run with these models. The licence entry is from memory.

name: RapidOCR (PP-OCRv6 default pipeline on ONNX Runtime; PP-OCRv5 script recognisers)
purpose: CPU OCR challenger to TOOL-382/383 for the OCR reference and second vote; the default wheel bundles PP-OCRv6 small det/rec models.
verification_evidence: 2026-10-05: Han recall 0.993 (best of all engines), Latin 0.971, Arabic 0.018, Devanagari 0.031 with the default pipeline; PP-OCRv5 arabic/devanagari recognisers 0.781 / 0.725; 7-11 s per page single-threaded (OBS-1102). Version and licence from PyPI (SRCH-1109).
rationale: Trial as the second OCR vote on Han pages only, where it beats tessdata_best chi_sim (0.993 vs 0.961, OBS-1102). Hold for Arabic and Devanagari: PP-OCRv6 has no models for them (SRCH-1121) and the PP-OCRv5 ones trail Tesseract by 15-16 points. About 3x slower than Tesseract per page.

name: PaddleOCR 3.7.0 (PP-OCRv6)
purpose: Upstream of RapidOCR's models; the newest PaddleOCR release, checked as a 2026 OCR challenger for non-Latin pages.
verification_evidence: Not installed (PaddlePaddle runtime not needed: RapidOCR runs the same PP-OCRv6 ONNX models, OBS-1102). Version and licence from PyPI (SRCH-1109); language coverage from SRCH-1121 search excerpts.
rationale: Hold for WP-3.2/3.5: search excerpts (SRCH-1121) report PP-OCRv6 recognisers for Chinese, English, Japanese and Latin-script languages but not Arabic or Devanagari, and the PP-OCRv6 pipeline run through RapidOCR recovered 1.8% / 3.1% of those pages (OBS-1102). Revisit if Arabic/Devanagari v6 models ship.

name: pdfrum (pure-Rust PDF library with damage recovery in pdfrum-parser)
purpose: Challenger to lopdf (TOOL-359) as the pure-Rust loader and text extractor, and a tolerant-reader baseline; its parser crate advertises damage recovery.
verification_evidence: 2026-10-05: all 1,100 REPDF files, no panics; beats lopdf 0.45.0 on C5 Print (recall 1.0 vs 0), C6 Save As (0.578 vs 0, precision 0.485), C9 (0.701 vs 0.645 Save As, 0.614 vs 0.463 Print); opens 0 of C1 and C10 (OBS-1103). crates.io: pdfrum-parser created 2026-09-08 (SRCH-1108).
rationale: Trial as a null-repair loader in WP-3.1 and as a challenger to lopdf's role. It recovers more text than lopdf on C5, C6 and C9 (OBS-1103), but its C6 text is less than half right (precision 0.485), so it is a plausible-but-wrong source that the metric suite must catch. Not an emitter candidate yet: its save/write path was not tested, the project is 4 weeks old, and it reports repair diagnostics on every file including originals, so diagnostics are not a damage signal. Its README says it uses PDFium as a read-only conformance oracle.

name: oxidize-pdf
purpose: Pure-Rust PDF toolkit (generation, parsing, manipulation, text extraction, PDF/A validation, per its crates.io description); a candidate emitter or loader beside lopdf.
verification_evidence: crates.io metadata only (SRCH-1108).
rationale: Untested. Listed because the sole-emitter assumption (lopdf) has not been compared against any maintained pure-Rust writer; run it through OBS-1103's probe and a round-trip save before any claim.

name: pdf_oxide
purpose: Pure-Rust PDF text extraction and editing library (Rust crate and PyPI wheel); a loader/extractor challenger.
verification_evidence: crates.io and PyPI metadata only (SRCH-1108, SRCH-1109). Its description claims a 100% pass rate on 3,830 real-world PDFs; unverified.
rationale: Untested. Its speed and pass-rate claims are self-reported on undamaged files; whether it tolerates C1/C4/C5/C10 is unknown. Cheap to add to OBS-1103's probe.

name: pdf-syntax (pdfluent)
purpose: Low-level PDF reading crate; same one-line description as hayro-syntax, relationship not checked.
verification_evidence: crates.io metadata only (SRCH-1108); created 2026-05-02, 1,798 recent downloads.
rationale: Hold: possibly a derivative of hayro-syntax (same description); no repository on a public forge in its metadata. Prefer hayro-syntax (TOOL-361) unless a distinct capability is shown.

name: krilla
purpose: High-level pure-Rust PDF writer (typst ecosystem); a candidate emitter if the product rebuilds documents rather than patching lopdf object graphs.
verification_evidence: crates.io metadata only (SRCH-1108).
rationale: Flags a product assumption, does not decide it: lopdf as the sole emitter has never been compared with a writer that generates conformant output from scratch. krilla writes new documents; it cannot pass through arbitrary existing objects, so it only fits a rebuild path (e.g. C4/C10 salvage).

name: pdf-writer
purpose: Low-level step-by-step pure-Rust PDF writer (typst); the layer under krilla.
verification_evidence: crates.io metadata only (SRCH-1108).
rationale: Same flag as TOOL-508: an emitter alternative for writing repaired objects with explicit control over serialization. Untested.

name: precomp2
purpose: Reversible preprocessing for compressed and container data (crates.io description); a possible alternative replay/recompression engine.
verification_evidence: crates.io metadata only (SRCH-1103, SRCH-1108).
rationale: Untested. Only worth a run if it reproduces Print to PDF streams, which neither stock zlib nor its exact ports do (OBS-1100, OBS-1101).

name: Cluster-aware selective risk certification (HG-CRC; document-level LTT)
purpose: Method for WP-3.12/3.13's auto-accept threshold when calibration rows (fields, streams, slots) are clustered within documents.
verification_evidence: Papers only: SRC-1105 (per-field certificates on clustered document fields; design effect 1.84-2.45, CLM-1106; field-iid premise is load-bearing, CLM-1107) and SRC-1106 (HG-CRC, CLM-1110, CLM-1111). No code run.
rationale: Challenges WP-3.12's '150 error-free slots' (CLM-1061) and how TOOL-470 is used. Split conformal needs exchangeable rows and LTT an i.i.d. calibration set (CLM-1100, CLM-1102); CRC holds only in expectation (CLM-1104) and a marginal guarantee can fail per group (CLM-1110). Our slots cluster by base document (CLM-1064): on document extraction the design effect is 1.84-2.45 (CLM-1106), so slot-iid certificates overstate the evidence about twofold (CLM-1107), while a document-iid certificate is near-vacuous at 800 documents (CLM-1108, CLM-1109). Inference: by the rule of three, certifying 2% at document level needs about 150 error-free documents, three times REPDF's 50 base documents. Use HG-CRC-style group guarantees (CLM-1111) or cluster-corrected bounds, and report the design effect; MAPIE stays the implementation of the plain case.

name: crepes
purpose: Conformal classifiers, regressors and predictive systems (PyPI summary); a MAPIE (TOOL-470) alternative with Mondrian (group-conditional) calibration.
verification_evidence: PyPI metadata only (SRCH-1109). Mondrian support is from memory.
rationale: Assess as a group-conditional alternative to TOOL-470; it does not by itself fix within-document dependence (TOOL-511). Mondrian capability from memory.

name: puncc
purpose: Predictive uncertainty calibration and conformalization library (PyPI summary); a MAPIE alternative.
verification_evidence: PyPI metadata only (SRCH-1109).
rationale: Hold: no capability beyond TOOL-470 identified for our case; listed so the alternatives search is on record.

name: poppler-science (LANL)
purpose: Poppler fork whose pdftotext adds per-glyph OCR (a small classifier) for glyphs with missing or broken Unicode mappings; a C6/C8-type recovery challenger.
verification_evidence: Found by SRCH-1123 (search excerpts and README). Not built. REPDF C7 and C8 keep no embedded font program anywhere in the file, and C8 no CMap stream either (OBS-1104).
rationale: Assess for real-world files with broken ToUnicode but intact fonts, as an external binary only (GPL). It cannot apply to REPDF C7/C8: glyph-shape recognition needs the glyph outlines, which those classes remove entirely (OBS-1104); the excerpts describe a Latin-centric model. No upset for C8.

name: pdf-cmap-fixer
purpose: Rebuilds ToUnicode maps from glyph names (search excerpt).
verification_evidence: SRCH-1123 excerpt only (repository created 2026-05).
rationale: Hold: glyph-name inference needs the font program or meaningful glyph names; REPDF C7/C8 remove every program (OBS-1104), and Print to PDF fonts are anonymous per-page instances (OBS-0907). Not an upset.

name: pdf-encoding-repair
purpose: Repairs garbled PDF text whose codes are shifted by a constant offset (PyPI description via search excerpt).
verification_evidence: SRCH-1123 excerpt.
rationale: Hold: constant-offset decoding covers a narrow failure; REPDF C6/C8 and the UDHR failures are not constant offsets (OBS-0906 needed a full substitution decipherer).

name: PDFix Font Fix
purpose: Commercial font/Unicode repair action (free Docker action; SDK proprietary), per search excerpt.
verification_evidence: SRCH-1123 excerpt.
rationale: Hold: proprietary and OCR-based; would need an account or vendor contact to evaluate, which this stage does not allow.

name: OnnxTR
purpose: docTR models on ONNX Runtime; a lighter CPU build of the second OCR vote (TOOL-383).
verification_evidence: PyPI metadata only (SRCH-1109).
rationale: Assess as a faster drop-in for docTR's 6-7 s per page if its outputs match TOOL-383's. Whether docTR's recognition vocabularies cover Arabic and Devanagari was not checked (from memory: they are Latin-oriented), so it may be a weak vote on those pages.

name: surya-ocr
purpose: Multilingual OCR and layout package; a 2026 OCR challenger.
license: Apache-2.0 (code, per PyPI); model weight terms not checked
verification_evidence: PyPI metadata only (SRCH-1109).
rationale: Not run: transformer OCR on 4 CPUs is likely slower than Tesseract per page (not measured), and weight licence terms were not checked. Worth one 24-page run with OBS-1102's script if WP-3.2 needs a third vote on Devanagari.
